How are the models fitted? Robust maximum likelihood (MLR), as in Chapters 6 and 7; only the four-wave models use standard maximum likelihood (Section 8.5). The models over several waves take hours, so all block models run in a script of their own; this chapter reads its results.

# Simultaneous block models of Chapter 8: per wave, over adjacent waves and
# over all four waves, for the three hypothesis blocks, and the saturated
# models behind the four-wave fit. Long: the models over several waves take
# hours. Each stage is saved as soon as it is done.
# Run from swt-website/ after Chapter 2:  Rscript scripts/block_models.R

source("R/packages.R")
source("R/settings.R")
source("R/measurement.R")
source("R/longitudinal_models.R")
source("R/block_models.R")
df      <- readRDS("cache/df.rds")      # one row per questionnaire (Chapter 2)
df_wide <- readRDS("cache/df_wide.rds") # one row per person (Chapter 2)

log_step <- \(...) cat(format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), ..., "\n")

# robust fit indices (MLR)
robust_fit <- \(fit) {
  fitMeasures(fit, c("chisq.scaled", "df", "cfi.robust", "rmsea.robust",
                     "srmr")) |>
    as.list() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    set_names(c("chisq", "df", "CFI", "RMSEA", "SRMR"))
}

# standard (ML) fit indices from the tests stored at fit time
standard_fit <- \(fit) {
  model    <- fit@test$standard
  baseline <- fit@baseline$test$standard
  n        <- lavInspect(fit, "ntotal")
  tibble(chisq = model$stat, df = model$df,
         CFI   = 1 - max(model$stat - model$df, 0) /
                   max(model$stat - model$df, baseline$stat - baseline$df, 0),
         RMSEA = sqrt(max(model$stat - model$df, 0) / (model$df * n)),
         SRMR  = as.numeric(fitMeasures(fit, "srmr")))
}

# convergence and admissibility, with the smallest eigenvalues of the latent
# correlations and of the residual covariances (negative: not positive
# definite)
admissibility <- \(fit) {
  theta <- lavInspect(fit, "theta")
  smallest_eigen <- \(m) min(eigen(m, only.values = TRUE)$values)
  tibble(converged  = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
         admissible = isTRUE(suppressWarnings(lavInspect(fit, "post.check"))),
         latent_eigen   = smallest_eigen(cov2cor(lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv"))),
         residual_eigen = smallest_eigen(theta),
         negative_residuals = sum(diag(theta) < 0))
}

# negative variances with their z-test: a negative estimate that does not
# differ from 0 is sampling error at the boundary (Kolenikov & Bollen, 2012)
negative_variances <- \(fit) {
  parameterEstimates(fit) |>
    filter(op == "~~", lhs == rhs, est < 0) |>
    select(variable = lhs, est, se, z, pvalue)
}

# latent correlations with 95 % CI
latent_r <- \(fit) {
  factors <- lavNames(fit, "lv")
  standardizedSolution(fit) |>
    filter(op == "~~", lhs != rhs, lhs %in% factors, rhs %in% factors) |>
    transmute(pair = str_c(lhs, " ~~ ", rhs), r = est.std, ci_low = ci.lower,
              ci_high = ci.upper)
}

# 1. one wave at a time
log_step("per wave")
per_wave <- expand_grid(block = names(blocks), wave = waves) |>
  mutate(fit = map2(block, wave, \(b, w) cfa(
           block_wave_model(blocks[[b]]),
           data = df |> filter(Occasion == w) |>
             select(all_of(items_of(blocks[[b]]))),
           estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml.x")),
         indices  = map(fit, robust_fit),
         checks   = map(fit, admissibility),
         negative = map(fit, negative_variances),
         r        = map(fit, latent_r),
         mi       = map(fit, \(f) modindices(f, sort. = TRUE) |>
                              filter(mi >= 20)))
saveRDS(select(per_wave, -fit), "cache/block_models_wave.rds")

# 2. adjacent waves: T0-T1, T1-T2, T2-T3
log_step("adjacent waves")
adjacent <- expand_grid(block = names(blocks),
                        window = list(c("T0", "T1"), c("T1", "T2"),
                                      c("T2", "T3")),
                        level = c("configural", "metric", "scalar")) |>
  mutate(window = map_chr(window, \(w) str_c(w, collapse = "-")))
adjacent <- adjacent |>
  mutate(fit = pmap(list(block, window, level), \(b, w, l) {
           log_step(b, w, l)
           cfa(block_long_model(blocks[[b]], l, over = str_split_1(w, "-")),
               data = df_wide, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml")
         }),
         indices  = map(fit, robust_fit),
         checks   = map(fit, admissibility),
         negative = map(fit, negative_variances))
saveRDS(select(adjacent, -fit), "cache/block_models_adjacent.rds")

# 3. the saturated model that the four-wave chi2 is measured against: does
# its EM estimate converge within the default 500 iterations, and how close
# to singular is its covariance matrix?
log_step("saturated models")
saturated_model <- \(b, iterations) {
  converged <- TRUE
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    cfa(block_long_model(blocks[[b]], "configural"), data = df_wide,
        estimator = "ML", missing = "fiml", do.fit = FALSE,
        em.h1.iter.max = iterations),
    warning = \(w) {
      if (str_detect(conditionMessage(w), "Maximum number of iterations"))
        converged <<- FALSE
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  h1 <- fit@h1  # the saturated model
  tibble(variables = length(lavNames(fit, "ov")),
         logl      = h1$logl$loglik,
         converged = converged,
         smallest_eigen = min(eigen(h1$implied$cov[[1]],
                                    only.values = TRUE)$values))
}
saturated <- expand_grid(block = names(blocks), iterations = c(500, 20000)) |>
  mutate(h1 = map2(block, iterations, saturated_model)) |>
  unnest(h1)
saveRDS(saturated, "cache/block_models_saturated.rds")

# 4. all four waves, with standard maximum likelihood (the robust
# corrections of MLR break down for models of this size) and enough EM
# iterations for the saturated model to converge (stage 3)
log_step("four waves")
four_waves <- expand_grid(block = names(blocks),
                          level = c("configural", "metric", "scalar")) |>
  mutate(fit = map2(block, level, \(b, l) {
           log_step(b, l)
           cfa(block_long_model(blocks[[b]], l), data = df_wide,
               estimator = "ML", missing = "fiml", em.h1.iter.max = 20000)
         }),
         indices  = map(fit, standard_fit),
         checks   = map(fit, admissibility),
         negative = map(fit, negative_variances))
saveRDS(select(four_waves, -fit), "cache/block_models_four.rds")
log_step("done")


per_wave   <- readRDS("cache/block_models_wave.rds")
adjacent   <- readRDS("cache/block_models_adjacent.rds")
four_waves <- readRDS("cache/block_models_four.rds")

Whether a block counts as invariant therefore turns on the configural model. Listening and Togetherness fits in all three windows (configural CFI 0.93 to 0.94) and is scalar invariant from wave to wave. Cognitive Complexity fits while the experimental group trains and during maintenance, but not while the control group trains (configural CFI 0.84). Well-being reaches the configural threshold only during maintenance (CFI 0.94, against 0.89 and 0.83 in the training windows), and none of its window models is admissible (Section 8.6).

title: 8. Simultaneous block models
text:
8.5 Invariance over all four waves
Does each block stay invariant over the whole year? The robust corrections of MLR break down for models of this size (the matrix they invert is singular for Well-being), so the four-wave models are fitted with standard maximum likelihood, again with full-information handling of missing answers.
What is the fit measured against? χ², CFI and RMSEA compare a model with the saturated model, which estimates every mean and covariance of the observed variables. With missing answers, the saturated model comes from the EM algorithm. title: 8. Simultaneous block models
text:
8.6 Admissibility
Are the solutions admissible? A solution is admissible when every variance is positive and both the latent correlations and the residual covariances form positive definite matrices. Large models with many freely correlated factors and thin overlap between waves are prone to solutions at this boundary (Chen et al., 2001). For each model that is not admissible, the smallest eigenvalue of the latent correlation matrix and of the residual covariance matrix (negative: not positive definite):

  per_wave   |> transmute(block, model = wave, checks, negative),
  adjacent   |> transmute(block, model = str_c(window, " ", level), checks,
                          negative),
  four_waves |> transmute(block, model = str_c("T0-T3 ", level), checks,
                          negative)
)

title: 9. Means and Δd
text:
9.3 The effects at a glance
How large and how precise is each effect? Δd with its 95 % interval (Δd ± 1.96 SE), by hypothesis block and window. Filled points are significant (p < .05), open points are not:

# readable names of the outcomes, the composites named by their hypothesis
outcome_labels <- c(set_names(scales$label, scales$scale),
                    H1_ListeningTogetherness = "Listening and Togetherness",
                    H2_CognitiveComplexity   = "Cognitive Complexity",
                    H3_Wellbeing             = "Well-being")

effects |>
  mutate(block   = coalesce(scales$block[match(outcome, scales$scale)],
                            "Composites") |>
                     factor(levels = c("H1", "H2", "H3", "Composites")),
         outcome = factor(outcome_labels[outcome],
                          levels = rev(outcome_labels[outcomes])),
         window  = str_replace(window, ": ", "\n"),
         ci_low  = delta_d - qnorm(.975) * se,
         ci_high = delta_d + qnorm(.975) * se,
         test    = if_else(p < .05, "p < .05", "p ≥ .05")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = delta_d, y = outcome, xmin = ci_low, xmax = ci_high,
             colour = test, fill = test)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = .3) +
  geom_linerange(linewidth = .5) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2.2, stroke = .6) +
  facet_grid(block ~ window, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("p < .05" = "grey15",
                                 "p ≥ .05" = "grey55")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("p < .05" = "grey15", "p ≥ .05" = "white")) +
  labs(x = "Δd, experimental minus control, with 95 % interval", y = NULL,
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = .2))








The intervals are wide: their median width grows from 0.44 units of Δd while the experimental group trains to 0.68 over the full year, as the pairs thin out. Single scales are therefore estimated loosely; the pattern across scales and windows carries more weight than any one interval.

title: 9. Means and Δd
text:
9.4 Another standard deviation
Does the result hold if d is divided by the SD of all questionnaires before the window? Above, change and standard deviation both come from the persons who answered at both waves. A common alternative divides each group’s change instead by the standard deviation of every questionnaire the group returned at the first wave of the window, whether or not the person answered again; the standard error stays that of the pairs. delta_d() does this with sd_pre = "all":

effects_all_sd <- effect_windows |>
  mutate(table = map2(pre, post, \(a, b)
    delta_d(df, a, b, outcomes, sd_pre = "all"))) |>
  unnest(table)

# both definitions side by side
sd_comparison <- effects |>
  select(window, outcome, delta_d, p) |>
  left_join(effects_all_sd |>
              select(window, outcome, delta_d_all = delta_d, p_all = p),
            by = c("window", "outcome"))

sd_comparison |>
  filter(outcome %in% scales$scale) |>
  summarise(significant_pairs_SD = sum(p < .05),
            significant_all_SD   = sum(p_all < .05),
            largest_shift        = round(max(abs(delta_d_all - delta_d)), 3),

title: 10. Multilevel models
text:
10.7 One-sided tests and many outcomes
Does the result hold if the tests are one-sided? The hypotheses are directional. The experimental group should gain more by T1 and keep its advantage at T2 (positive interactions, 10.2); the control group should gain more while it trains (negative terms in the period-specific model and in the second term of the piecewise model, 10.3), while the first piecewise term should be positive. A one-sided test looks only in the expected direction: it halves the p of an effect that points there and gives an effect against the expectation a p above .5. The tests above stay two-sided.

# the directional tests of 10.2 and 10.3, with the sign they expect
directional <- bind_rows(
  interactions |>
    filter(wave %in% c("T1", "T2")) |>
    transmute(test = str_c("preregistered, ", wave), outcome, b, se, df, p,
              expected = 1),
  period_specific |>
    transmute(test = "period-specific, T3", outcome, b, se, df, p,
              expected = -1),
  piecewise |>

              b, se, df, p,
              expected = if_else(training == "experimental", 1, -1))
) |>
  mutate(p_one_sided = pt(expected * b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE))

title: 7. Measurement invariance over time
text:
7.5 Partial invariance
How far does partial invariance reach where a step fails? Three steps fail under at least one set of cutoffs: the scalar steps of I Listen and Tolerance Diversity, and the metric step of Autonomy Satisfaction under the small-sample cutoffs. For each, the loadings (metric step) or the intercepts (scalar step) of one item are freed at every wave, first the item whose equality constraints have the largest score test, and the model is fitted again, until the step holds. The search stops before fewer than two items would keep equal parameters, the minimum for comparing latent means (Byrne et al., 1989). Loadings freed at the metric step stay free at the scalar step.

# the equality constraints of a fit, with the item and the kind of
# parameter (loading or intercept) each one binds
constraint_items <- \(fit) {
  parameters <- parTable(fit) |>
    select(plabel, bound_op = op, bound_lhs = lhs, bound_rhs = rhs)
  parTable(fit) |>
    filter(op == "==") |>
    mutate(index = row_number()) |>
    left_join(parameters, by = c(rhs = "plabel")) |>
    transmute(index,
              parameter = if_else(bound_op == "=~", "loading", "intercept"),
              item      = if_else(bound_op == "=~", bound_rhs, bound_lhs) |>
                str_remove("_T[0-3]$"))
}

# the item whose loadings or intercepts, freed at every wave, would improve
# the fit most: the largest score test of its constraints taken together
largest_score <- \(fit, parameter) {
  constraint_items(fit) |>
    filter(parameter == .env$parameter) |>
    summarise(X2 = lavTestScore(fit, release = index,
                                univariate = FALSE)$test$X2,
              .by = item) |>
    slice_max(X2, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    pull(item)
}

# the two sets of cutoffs: Chen's for more than 300 persons (as in steps())
# and those for 300 or fewer (holds_small() above)
holds_chen <- \(level, delta_CFI, delta_RMSEA, delta_SRMR) {
  delta_CFI >= -.010 & delta_RMSEA <= .015
}
cutoffs <- list(Chen = holds_chen, small_sample = holds_small)

# free one item after the other until the step holds, or until only two
# items would keep equal parameters
free_until_holds <- \(construct, level, before, holds,
                      free_loading = character(), freed = character()) {
  fit <- fit_longitudinal(invariance_model(
    construct, level,
    free_loading   = if (level == "metric") freed else free_loading,
    free_intercept = if (level == "scalar") freed))
  change <- fit_indices(fit) - fit_indices(before)
  done   <- holds(level, change$CFI, change$RMSEA, change$SRMR)
  if (done || length(freed) == length(model_items[[construct]]) - 2) {
    return(tibble(level, freed = list(freed), delta_CFI = change$CFI,
                  delta_RMSEA = change$RMSEA, delta_SRMR = change$SRMR,
                  holds = done, fit = list(fit)))
  }
  parameter <- if (level == "metric") "loading" else "intercept"
  free_until_holds(construct, level, before, holds, free_loading,
                   c(freed, largest_score(fit, parameter)))
}

# both steps of a construct under one set of cutoffs
partial_steps <- \(construct, set) {
  configural <- invariance |>
    filter(construct == .env$construct, level == "configural") |>
    pull(fit) |>
    pluck(1)
  metric <- free_until_holds(construct, "metric", configural, cutoffs[[set]])
  scalar <- free_until_holds(construct, "scalar", metric$fit[[1]],
                             cutoffs[[set]], free_loading = metric$freed[[1]])
  bind_rows(metric, scalar) |>
    mutate(construct, set, .before = 1)
}

# the constructs with a failing step, per set of cutoffs
failing_steps <- invariance_small |>
  filter(level != "configural") |>
  select(construct, Chen = holds, small_sample = holds_small) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Chen, small_sample), names_to = "set",
               values_to = "holds") |>
  filter(!holds) |>
  distinct(construct = as.character(construct), set)

partial <- failing_steps |>
  mutate(steps = map2(construct, set, partial_steps)) |>
  select(steps) |>
  unnest(steps)

partial |>
  mutate(freed = map_chr(freed, \(items)
    if (length(items) == 0) "none" else str_flatten_comma(items))) |>
  select(-fit) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))

title: 7. Measurement invariance over time
section: 7.6 The same measurement in both groups
text:
7.6 The same measurement in both groups
Do the two groups answer alike before the training? Chapter 11 holds the loadings and intercepts equal not only over the waves but also over the two groups. Before the training, at T0, this can be tested directly: one factor model per construct on the January questionnaires, in two groups (Control and Experimental), with the same three levels across the groups and both sets of cutoffs. Two-item constructs are again tau-equivalent, with the factor variance 1 in the control group (free in the experimental group from the metric level on), so that only their scalar step tests anything. Constructs with two or three items have a saturated configural model (df = 0), which fits perfectly. Because these models have few degrees of freedom, each step also shows the scaled χ² difference test.

t0_questionnaires <- df |> filter(Occasion == "T0")

# one construct at T0 in two groups; two items load equally
# (tau-equivalent), with the factor variance 1 in the control group and,
# from the metric level on, free in the experimental group
group_model <- \(construct, level) {
  items <- model_items[[construct]]
  pairs <- residual_pairs |> filter(construct == .env$construct)
  if (length(items) == 2) {
    loading  <- if (level == "configural") "c(L1, L2)*" else "L*"
    variance <- if (level == "configural") "c(1, 1)" else "c(1, NA)"
    return(str_c("F =~ NA*", items[1], " + ",
                 str_c(loading, items, collapse = " + "),
                 "\nF ~~ ", variance, "*F"))
  }
  c(str_c("F =~ ", str_c(items, collapse = " + ")),
    str_c(pairs$item_a, " ~~ ", pairs$item_b)) |>
    str_c(collapse = "\n")
}

# what each level holds equal across the groups
group_equal <- list(configural = character(), metric = "loadings",
                    scalar = c("loadings", "intercepts"))

group_invariance <- expand_grid(construct = names(model_items),
                                level     = invariance_levels) |>
  mutate(fit = map2(construct, level, \(c, l) cfa(
    group_model(c, l), data = t0_questionnaires, group = "condition",
    group.equal = group_equal[[l]], estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml")))

# the scaled χ² difference test of a step; none for the configural level,
# for a step that adds no constraint, and when a model has no scaled χ²
difference_p <- \(fit, before) {
  if (is.null(before)) return(NA_real_)
  scaled <- c(fitMeasures(fit, "chisq.scaled"),
              fitMeasures(before, "chisq.scaled"))
  if (fitMeasures(fit, "df") == fitMeasures(before, "df") || anyNA(scaled)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  lavTestLRT(before, fit, method = "satorra.bentler.2001")[2, "Pr(>Chisq)"]
}

group_steps <- group_invariance |>
  mutate(indices = map(fit, fit_indices),
         p       = map2_dbl(fit, lag(fit), difference_p),
         .by = construct) |>
  unnest(indices) |>
  # a saturated model (df = 0) fits perfectly
  mutate(CFI   = if_else(df == 0, 1, CFI),
         RMSEA = if_else(df == 0, 0, RMSEA)) |>
  mutate(delta_CFI   = CFI - lag(CFI),
         delta_RMSEA = RMSEA - lag(RMSEA),
         delta_SRMR  = SRMR - lag(SRMR),
         .by = construct) |>
  mutate(holds = if_else(level == "configural", CFI >= .90,
                         holds_chen(level, delta_CFI, delta_RMSEA,
                                    delta_SRMR)),
         holds_small = if_else(level == "configural", CFI >= .90,
                               holds_small(level, delta_CFI, delta_RMSEA,
                                           delta_SRMR)))

# the level a construct reaches: the highest step that holds together with
# the steps before it
level_reached <- \(metric, scalar) {
  case_when(!metric ~ "configural", !scalar ~ "metric", .default = "scalar")
}

group_summary <- group_steps |>
  filter(level != "configural") |>
  select(construct, level, delta_CFI, delta_RMSEA, p, holds, holds_small) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from  = level,
              values_from = c(delta_CFI, delta_RMSEA, p, holds, holds_small),
              names_glue  = "{level}_{.value}") |>
  mutate(Chen         = level_reached(metric_holds, scalar_holds),
         small_sample = level_reached(metric_holds_small,
                                      scalar_holds_small))

group_summary |>
  select(construct, metric_delta_CFI, metric_delta_RMSEA, metric_p,
         scalar_delta_CFI, scalar_delta_RMSEA, scalar_p, Chen,
         small_sample) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))

Before the training, 13 of the 22 constructs reach scalar invariance across the groups, under both sets of cutoffs alike. Of the 11 failing steps, 6 fail on the RMSEA alone: with saturated or nearly saturated configural models, a step that adds two or three constraints moves the RMSEA far from 0 even when the χ² difference is not significant (Belongingness, metric step: ΔRMSEA = .085, p = .146); in models with few degrees of freedom the RMSEA is known to be unstable (Kenny, Kaniskan & McCoach, 2015). The χ² difference test rejects equal loadings for Rogerian Schema and Tolerance Diversity and equal intercepts for Paradox Mindset and Empowerment. Women Attitude’s configural model at T0 has a negative residual variance and no scaled χ², so its first test is missing.
For the difference-in-differences of Chapter 11, a difference between the groups that stays the same over the waves matters less than a change over time: it shifts every latent mean of a group alike and drops out of the change within the group. Different loadings matter more, because they set the unit in which each group’s change is measured; the χ² test and the CFI agree on different loadings for Rogerian Schema and Tolerance Diversity.

title: 7. Measurement invariance over time
text:
7.7 Approximate invariance
How far are the waves from invariance when nothing is held equal, and does it move the latent means? Besides the tests above, the preregistration names approximate invariance by alignment (Asparouhov & Muthén, 2014), as implemented in the package sirt. Alignment starts from the configural model, with the factor standardised at each wave, and searches the latent means and standard deviations under which the loadings and intercepts of the four waves are as alike as possible, without forcing them to be equal. Two results per construct: the share of loadings and of intercepts that lie more than .10 item standard deviations from their common aligned value (noninvariant), and how far the aligned means of T1 to T3 lie from those of the scalar model, both in standard deviations of the factor at T0. Asparouhov and Muthén (2014) trust aligned means when no more than 25 % of the parameters are noninvariant. Their R² measures need many groups; with four waves they rest on four values per parameter and are left out.

# loadings (factor variance 1 at every wave) and intercepts of the
# configural model, waves in rows, in standard deviations of each item;
# each wave weighs with the root of the persons who answered the item
configural_parameters <- \(construct) {
  items <- model_items[[construct]]
  item_sd <- map_dbl(items, \(item) sd(df[[item]], na.rm = TRUE))
  solution <- invariance |>
    filter(construct == .env$construct, level == "configural") |>
    pull(fit) |>
    pluck(1) |>
    standardizedSolution(type = "std.lv")
  in_item_sd <- \(type) solution |>
    filter(op == type, op == "=~" | !str_starts(lhs, "F_")) |>
    mutate(variable = if_else(op == "=~", rhs, lhs),
           wave     = str_extract(variable, "T[0-3]$"),
           item     = str_remove(variable, "_T[0-3]$")) |>
    select(wave, item, est.std) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = item, values_from = est.std) |>
    arrange(wave) |>
    select(all_of(items)) |>
    as.matrix() |>
    sweep(2, item_sd, "/")
  answered <- map(waves, \(w) colSums(!is.na(df_wide[at(items, w)])))
  list(lambda = in_item_sd("=~"), nu = in_item_sd("~1"),
       weights = sqrt(do.call(rbind, answered)))
}

# the latent means of T1 to T3 in the scalar model, in T0 standard
# deviations
scalar_means <- \(construct) {
  fit <- invariance |>
    filter(construct == .env$construct, level == "scalar") |>
    pull(fit) |>
    pluck(1)
  lavInspect(fit, "mean.lv")[-1] /
    sqrt(lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv")["F_T0", "F_T0"])
}

alignment <- tibble(construct = names(model_items)) |>
  mutate(parameters = map(construct, configural_parameters),
         aligned    = map(parameters, \(p) invariance.alignment(
           lambda = p$lambda, nu = p$nu, wgt = p$weights)),
         # noninvariant: more than .10 item SD from the common value
         tolerance  = map(aligned, \(a) invariance_alignment_constraints(
           a, lambda_parm_tol = .10, nu_parm_tol = .10)),
         pct_loadings    = map_dbl(tolerance,
                                   \(t) t$lambda_list$prop_noninvariance),
         pct_intercepts  = map_dbl(tolerance,
                                   \(t) t$nu_list$prop_noninvariance),
         mean_difference = map2_dbl(aligned, construct, \(a, c)
           max(abs(a$pars$alpha0[-1] - scalar_means(c)))))

  select(construct, pct_loadings, pct_intercepts, mean_difference) |>

title: 11. Latent difference-in-differences
text:
11.8 Level means outside the training
Do the latent means stay level outside each group’s own training? The design suggests a sparer model: the control group keeps its January level until its own training (T0 = T1 = T2), and the experimental group keeps the level it reached after its own training (T1 = T2 = T3). These four equality constraints on the latent means are tested against the free model by the scaled χ² difference (Satorra & Bentler, 2001). Fitting all models again, restricted and on the sample sets of 11.9, takes a while, so these models run in a script of their own; this chapter reads its results.

# Sensitivity of the latent difference-in-differences of Chapter 11: the
# restricted model with level means outside the training, and the models of
# all 22 constructs on the sample sets S0 to S9. Each stage is saved as soon
# as it is done.
# Run from swt-website/ after Chapters 4 and 7:
#   Rscript scripts/latent_did_sensitivity.R

source("R/packages.R")
source("R/settings.R")
source("R/measurement.R")
source("R/longitudinal_models.R")
source("R/smm_model.R")
df       <- readRDS("cache/df.rds")       # one row per questionnaire (Ch. 2)
df_wide  <- readRDS("cache/df_wide.rds")  # one row per person (Chapter 2)
careless <- readRDS("cache/careless.rds") # flags S8, S9 (Chapter 4)
item_names <- names(select(df, ListenOther1:CompetenceNonFrustrated4))

log_step <- \(...) cat(format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), ..., "\n")

# convergence and admissibility of a fit
checks <- \(fit) {
  tibble(converged  = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
         admissible = isTRUE(suppressWarnings(lavInspect(fit, "post.check"))))
}

# the estimates of all labelled parameters of a model (as in Chapter 11)
estimates <- \(fit) {
  parameterEstimates(fit) |>
    filter(label != "") |>
    distinct(label, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    select(label, est, se, z, pvalue) |>
    as_tibble()
}

# a fit index as a plain number
index <- \(fit, name) as.numeric(fitMeasures(fit, name))

# Stage 1: the restricted model. The control group keeps its level until
# its own training (T0 = T1 = T2), the experimental group keeps the level
# it reached after its own (T1 = T2 = T3): four constraints on the latent
# means, tested against the free model by the scaled χ² difference
# (Satorra & Bentler, 2001).
restricted_means <- c("m_con_T0 == m_con_T1", "m_con_T1 == m_con_T2",
                      "m_exp_T1 == m_exp_T2", "m_exp_T2 == m_exp_T3")

# the free and the restricted model of a construct and their comparison
restriction_test <- \(construct) {
  log_step("restricted means:", construct)
  free       <- fit_smm(smm_model(construct))
  restricted <- fit_smm(str_c(c(smm_model(construct), restricted_means),
                              collapse = "\n"))
  test <- lavTestLRT(free, restricted, method = "satorra.bentler.2001")
  tibble(chisq_free       = index(free, "chisq.scaled"),
         df_free          = index(free, "df"),
         chisq_restricted = index(restricted, "chisq.scaled"),
         df_restricted    = index(restricted, "df"),
         delta_chisq      = test[2, "Chisq diff"],
         delta_df         = test[2, "Df diff"],
         p                = test[2, "Pr(>Chisq)"]) |>
    bind_cols(checks(restricted))
}

restricted <- tibble(construct = names(model_items)) |>
  mutate(test = map(construct, \(c) suppressWarnings(restriction_test(c)))) |>
  unnest(test)
saveRDS(restricted, "cache/latent_did_restricted.rds")

# Stage 2: the sample sets of Chapter 14 (S7 equals S0, Chapter 1)
df <- df |>
  left_join(select(careless, id, Occasion, s8_no_careless,
                   s9_no_careless_strict),
            by = c("id", "Occasion"))

sample_sets <- tribble(
  ~set, ~flag,
  "S0", NA,
  "S1", "s1_complete",
  "S2", "s2_no_singletons",
  "S3", "s3_has_T0",
  "S4", "s4_T0_plus_post",
  "S5", "s5_group_baseline",
  "S6", "s6_no_T0_dropouts",
  "S8", "s8_no_careless",
  "S9", "s9_no_careless_strict"
)

# the wide data of a set: the questionnaires it keeps, side by side as in
# Chapter 2, with each person's covariates; persons without a questionnaire
# in the set drop out
set_wide <- \(flag) {
  kept <- if (is.na(flag)) df else filter(df, .data[[flag]])
  kept |>
    select(id, condition, Occasion, all_of(item_names)) |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols     = c(id, condition),
                names_from  = Occasion,
                values_from = all_of(item_names),
                names_glue  = "{.value}_{Occasion}") |>
    left_join(select(df_wide, id, age_c, female), by = "id")
}

# the model of a construct on the data of a set
set_model <- \(set, data, construct) {
  log_step(set, construct)
  fit <- suppressWarnings(fit_smm(smm_model(construct), data = data))
  checks(fit) |>
    mutate(control      = lavInspect(fit, "nobs")[1],
           experimental = lavInspect(fit, "nobs")[2],
           estimates    = list(estimates(fit)))
}

latent_sets <- sample_sets |>
  mutate(data = map(flag, set_wide)) |>
  cross_join(tibble(construct = names(model_items))) |>
  mutate(model = pmap(list(set, data, construct), set_model)) |>
  select(set, construct, model) |>
  unnest(model)
saveRDS(latent_sets, "cache/latent_did_sets.rds")
log_step("done")

title: 12. Serial mediation
text:
12.5 Latent blocks
Does the result hold if measurement error is modelled? The composites of 12.1 treat each block as if it were measured without error. A structural-after-measurement model (SAM; Rosseel & Loh, 2024) first estimates how the scales measure each block and then the paths between the latent blocks; in its local form, misfit in one measurement model does not spread to the other blocks, as it would in a joint model. Each block is a latent factor measured by its scale scores, eight for H1, five for H2 and ten for H3, at both waves of a window. Scale scores rather than items keep the measurement models small (46 indicators instead of 200) and stay close to the composites, which average the same items. Within a block, each loading is equal at the two waves (over two adjacent waves, equal loadings cost the blocks almost no fit; Chapter 8), each scale’s residual covaries with itself over the waves, and the residuals of the scales made only of reverse-keyed items covary within a wave, for their shared wording (No Alienation and No Isolation in H1, the three non-frustration scales in H3; Chapter 5). The structural part is the model of 12.1, with its labels and effects. The functions:

# Serial mediation with latent blocks (Chapter 12): each hypothesis block is
# a latent factor measured by its scale scores, estimated by local
# structural-after-measurement (SAM; Rosseel & Loh, 2024). Needs R/scales.R
# and R/mediation_model.R.

# one row per person, in the order of df_wide: the 23 scale scores at each
# wave (ListenOther_T0, ...) and the two training indicators
scale_scores_wide <- \(data, wide) {
  scores <- data |>
    select(id, Occasion, all_of(scales$scale)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Occasion, values_from = all_of(scales$scale),
                names_glue = "{.value}_{Occasion}")
  wide |>
    select(id, train_eg, train_cg) |>
    left_join(scores, by = "id")
}

sam_blocks <- list(H1 = h1_scales, H2 = h2_scales, H3 = h3_scales)

# scales of reverse-keyed items only: their residuals share the wording
reverse_keyed <- c("NoAlienation", "NoIsolation", "AutonomyNonFrustrated",
                   "RelatednessNonFrustrated", "CompetenceNonFrustrated")

# one block at the two waves of a window: the first scale is the marker,
# the loadings are equal over the two waves, each scale's residual covaries
# with itself over the waves and with the other reverse-keyed scales
measurement_block <- \(block, waves) {
  s      <- sam_blocks[[block]]
  labels <- c("1*", str_c(str_to_lower(block), "_", seq_along(s)[-1], "*"))
  keyed  <- intersect(s, reverse_keyed)
  wording <- if (length(keyed) < 2) character() else
    map(waves, \(w) combn(keyed, 2, \(p)
      str_c(p[1], "_", w, " ~~ ", p[2], "_", w))) |> unlist()
  c(map_chr(waves, \(w) str_c(block, "_", w, " =~ ",
                              str_c(labels, s, "_", w, collapse = " + "))),
    str_c(s, "_", waves[1], " ~~ ", s, "_", waves[2]),
    wording)
}

# the measurement blocks and the structural model of 12.1, with the
# composites replaced by the latent blocks (T1_Hypothesis2_... -> H2_T1)
sam_mediation_model <- \(pre, post, treated) {
  structural <- mediation_model(pre, post, treated) |>
    str_replace_all("(T[0-3])_Hypothesis([1-3])_[A-Za-z]+", "H\\2_\\1")
  c(map(names(sam_blocks), \(b) measurement_block(b, c(pre, post))) |>
      unlist(),
    structural) |>
    str_c(collapse = "\n")
}

# the measurement blocks of a window: each block at both waves together
sam_mm_list <- \(pre, post) {
  map(names(sam_blocks), \(b) str_c(b, "_", c(pre, post))) |>
    set_names(names(sam_blocks))
}

# local SAM, missing values by full information (with enough EM steps for
# the saturated moments, as in Chapter 8), 1,000 bootstrap draws (seed as
# in Chapter 12)
fit_sam_mediation <- \(model, data, pre, post) {
  set.seed(20260525)
  sam(model, data = data, mm.list = sam_mm_list(pre, post),
      missing = "fiml", em.h1.iter.max = 20000, se = "bootstrap",
      bootstrap.args = list(R = 1000L))
}

# the fit of each measurement block, the first step of SAM on its own
measurement_fit <- \(model, data, pre, post) {
  steps <- sam(model, data = data, mm.list = sam_mm_list(pre, post),
               missing = "fiml", em.h1.iter.max = 20000, se = "none",
               output = "list")
  steps$MM.FIT |>
    set_names(names(sam_blocks)) |>
    map(\(f) fitMeasures(f, c("chisq", "df", "cfi", "rmsea", "srmr")) |>
          as.list() |>
          as_tibble()) |>
    list_rbind(names_to = "block")
}

# quantiles of bootstrap draws, interpolated on the normal scale between
# neighbouring order statistics (as lavaan's percentile intervals)
draw_quantile <- \(draws, probs) {
  t <- sort(draws[is.finite(draws)])
  n <- length(t)
  map_dbl(probs, \(p) {
    k <- trunc((n + 1) * p)
    if (k < 1) return(t[1])
    if (k >= n) return(t[n])
    z <- qnorm(c(p, k / (n + 1), (k + 1) / (n + 1)))
    t[k] + (z[1] - z[2]) / (z[3] - z[2]) * (t[k + 1] - t[k])
  })
}

# the bias-corrected percentile interval of bootstrap draws, computed as
# lavaan's boot.ci.type = "bca.simple"
bc_interval <- \(draws, estimate, level = .95) {
  z0 <- qnorm(mean(draws < estimate))
  draw_quantile(draws, pnorm(2 * z0 + qnorm((1 + c(-level, level)) / 2)))
}

# the defined effects of a SAM fit: each effect's formula (A*B1*C1, ...) on
# the estimates and on every bootstrap draw
sam_effects <- \(fit) {
  draws <- as.data.frame(lavInspect(fit, "boot"))
  parameterEstimates(fit, se = FALSE, zstat = FALSE, pvalue = FALSE,
                     ci = FALSE) |>
    filter(op == ":=") |>
    mutate(ci = map2(rhs, est, \(f, e)
      bc_interval(eval(str2lang(f), draws), e))) |>
    transmute(effect = label, est, ci_low = map_dbl(ci, 1),
              ci_high = map_dbl(ci, 2))
}

With latent blocks, the total indirect effect on well-being carries in both training windows and is larger than with the composites (β = 0.17 against 0.08 while the experimental group trains, 0.21 against 0.12 while the control group trains); between the trainings it does not carry, as with the composites. Within it, the weight moves to the serial path, which carries in both training windows (β = 0.11 and 0.07, against 0.01 and 0.02), while the paths through H1 alone and through H2 alone no longer carry in Model 1, nor the path through H2 alone in Model 4. Freed of measurement error, the blocks correlate more closely (H1 with H2 at T1: r = .64, against .46 for the composites), and more of the way from the training to well-being runs through both mediators in series. The direct path is not significant in any window; the total effect on well-being, not significant with the composites while the experimental group trains, carries with latent blocks (β = 0.13).
The latent estimates are less precise. The paths into well-being rest on latent predictors that correlate closely (H2 at the start and at the end of Model 1: r = .75), the intervals are wider, and 12 of the 4,000 bootstrap draws (3, 8, 1 and 0 in the four windows) end in a solution that is not admissible. The latent model thus confirms the total indirect effect and the serial path in both training windows; it does not confirm how 12.3 splits the indirect effect into single paths.

title: 19. Training effects on the new structure
section: 19.6 Invariance of the two factors over time
text:
19.6 Invariance of the two factors over time
Can the latent means of the two factors be compared over the waves? A latent difference-in-differences (Chapter 11) compares latent means, and that needs scalar invariance over the waves (Chapter 7). Each factor gets the longitudinal model of Chapter 7, with its community scores as indicators: one factor per wave, the first community as the marker, the four factors correlated, and each community’s residual correlated with itself over the waves (factor_invariance_model() in 19.1). The rule is that of Chapter 7 (Chen, 2007): a level holds when the robust CFI drops by no more than .010 and the robust RMSEA rises by no more than .015.

communities_wide <- community_scores_wide(df, df_wide)

factor_invariance <- expand_grid(
  factor = c("engagement", "wellbeing_agency"),
  level  = c("configural", "metric", "scalar")
) |>
  mutate(fit = map2(factor, level, \(f, l)
    fit_longitudinal(factor_invariance_model(f, l), communities_wide)),
    admissible = map_lgl(fit, \(f) suppressWarnings(
      lavInspect(f, "post.check"))))

fit_indices <- \(fit) {
  fitMeasures(fit, c("chisq.scaled", "df", "cfi.robust", "rmsea.robust",
                     "srmr")) |>
    as.list() |>
    as_tibble() |>
    set_names(c("chisq", "df", "CFI", "RMSEA", "SRMR"))
}

factor_steps <- factor_invariance |>
  mutate(indices = map(fit, fit_indices)) |>
  unnest(indices) |>
  select(-fit) |>
  mutate(delta_CFI   = CFI - lag(CFI),
         delta_RMSEA = RMSEA - lag(RMSEA),
         holds       = if_else(is.na(delta_CFI), CFI >= .90,
                               delta_CFI >= -.010 & delta_RMSEA <= .015),
         .by = factor)

factor_steps |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))

Both configural models fit well (robust CFI .963 and 1.000). Engagement keeps its loadings over the waves (metric: ΔCFI = .001), but not its intercepts (scalar: ΔCFI = -.020): its communities do not all shift by the same amount from wave to wave. Well-being and agency fails the metric step on the RMSEA alone, which rises from 0 in the configural model by .020 (ΔCFI = -.004); the equal intercepts add no misfit beyond that (scalar against metric: ΔCFI = .003). Under the rule of Chapter 7, neither factor is scalar invariant over the four waves, so their latent means cannot be compared over time, and no latent difference-in-differences is estimated on them. Their training effects rest on the manifest scores of 19.2 to 19.5.

title: 24. Requests and their status
text:
NoteAbout this chapter



What the team asked for in its e-mails about the analyses and about this documentation, from June 2025 to November 2026, and where each request stands now. The list was compiled from the e-mails and checked against the chapters of this documentation. Organisational matters and the wording of the paper are not part of it; requests about the paper are only summarised at the end. Computes nothing.

title: 24. Requests and their status
text:
24.1 How the list was made
Where do the requests come from? The team discussed the analyses in 52 e-mail threads between June 2025 and November 2026. Every request in them was noted, 269 in all: questions, proposals, corrections and the tasks of the work plans.
Which requests are left out? Of these, 56 were organisational, about travel, funding, meetings and submissions; they are left out. Another 49 concern the paper rather than this documentation, such as the text of its sections, its figures or the literature; they are summarised in 24.14. Each of the other 164 requests was checked against the chapters: is the analysis there, in which section, and in the form that was asked for?
How is a request written here? In one plain sentence, in the words of this documentation rather than those of the e-mail. Requests that ask for the same thing share a row. The column Where names the section, for example 9.3 for Chapter 9, Section 3; a dash marks a request that concerns the whole documentation or that no section answers.

title: 24. Requests and their status
text:
24.13 Decisions that remain open
Which choices are still to be made? For six questions the documentation shows the alternatives side by side, so that the team can decide with the results in view:

Cutoffs for invariance. Whether the conventional cutoffs or the stricter ones for small samples decide; the verdicts differ for a single construct (Chapter 7.3).
Multiple testing and one-sided tests. Whether the results are corrected for testing many scales at once, and whether they are tested one-sided, as the directional hypotheses would allow (Chapters 9.5, 10.7 and 11.4).
The standard deviation of Δd. Whether Δd is standardized by the persons who answered at both waves of a window or by all questionnaires before it; the choice matters mainly for the replication while the control group trains (Chapter 9.4).
Trainers in the multilevel models. Whether the models include the trainers as a level, as preregistered, although the trainers add almost nothing and change no verdict (Chapters 10.2 and 10.6).
Latent models at a boundary and missing covariates. How to treat the seven latent models with an estimate at an impossible value, such as a negative variance, and the 23 persons without age or sex, who are not part of the latent comparisons (Chapter 11.2).
Post hoc factors. How to report the effects on the two post hoc factors, which are not measured alike at all four waves, so that their effects rest on manifest scores only (Chapter 19.6).

title: 24. Requests and their status
text:
24.14 Requests about the paper
What did the team ask about the paper? Of the 213 requests, 49 concern the paper or the work on it rather than this documentation. Most are about its text, from the introduction to the discussion and the choice of journal (19), its figures and tables, among them the table of deviations from the preregistration (8), and the literature (6); seven concern the qualitative part of the study, which this documentation does not cover, and nine how tasks and files were shared within the team. Where they need numbers, these come from the chapters that Chapter 0 assigns to each part of the paper.
